summary: Practice reading JavaScript arrays and building new ones with loops, map and filter.

lessons.title: Reading an array and looping over it

pages.title: Indexes and .length
pages.body_md: An array keeps items in order. Read one item by its **index**, counting from 0, and get the item count from `.length`.

examples.note: Indexes start at 0, so the last index is one less than the length.

pages.title: for...of loops
pages.body_md: A `for...of` loop runs its body once for every item in the array, in order.

examples.note: A variable outside the loop collects the result.

pages.title: .map()
pages.body_md: `.map(fn)` calls `fn` on every item and returns a new array of the results. The original array is left as it was.

examples.note: The arrow function says what each item becomes.

pages.title: .filter()
pages.body_md: `.filter(fn)` keeps the items for which `fn` returns true, in a new array.

examples.note: Items for which the test is false are left out.

exercises.title: Last item
exercises.prompt_md: Write `lastItem(items)`. It takes a non-empty array and returns its last item.
exercises.hint_md: The index of the last item depends on how many items there are.

exercises.title: Count long words
exercises.prompt_md: Write `countLong(words, n)`. It returns how many strings in `words` have more than `n` characters.
exercises.hint_md: Keep a counter outside a loop over the words and add one for each word that is long enough.

exercises.title: Double everything
exercises.prompt_md: Write `doubleAll(nums)`. It returns a new array with every number in `nums` multiplied by 2, in the same order.
exercises.hint_md: One array method turns each item into a new value and gives back the new array.

exercises.title: Squares of the even numbers
exercises.prompt_md: Write `evenSquares(nums)`. It returns the squares of the even numbers in `nums`, in their original order. Odd numbers are left out.
exercises.hint_md: First keep only the numbers you want, then change each one.
